_about: The draft demo video, scene by scene. scripts/demo/record.mjs speaks each line with the macOS voice, records the live app doing the matching steps, and builds demo/AppealPath-demo.mp4. The live read decides which 'correct' line plays: correctMissing if the reader found no deadline, correctFax if the second reader flags the phone as a fax number, correctOk if everything matches. Replace the voice with your own by recording over demo/AppealPath-demo-silent.mp4.

scenes.label: AppealPath
scenes.text: This is AppealPath. When health insurance denies care, you get a letter full of codes and fine print, and a deadline that's easy to miss. AppealPath turns that letter into one clear next step. Every letter in this video is fictional.

scenes.label: 1 · Your letter
scenes.text: Here's a simulated phone photo of a fictional denial letter. I add the photo and answer five quick questions: a Marketplace plan, the care already happened, and I live in Missouri.

scenes.label: 2 · Check what we read
scenes.text: The AI reads the letter live and copies what's printed: what was denied, why, the deadline, and who to call. Then a second reader, running on the phone, checks the deadline, the reason and the phone number against the photo.

scenes.label: 2 · Fix what's wrong
scenes.text: And it caught a real mistake: the AI picked the fax number as the phone number. In testing, the AI even said it was one hundred percent sure of a sentence it had copied wrong, so AppealPath never trusts its confidence. The highlight shows where the number is printed, and I fix it before going on.

scenes.label: 2 · Fix what's missing
scenes.text: On this photo the AI couldn't find the deadline, and it won't make one up. So I type it exactly as it's printed on the letter, and AppealPath uses my words.

scenes.label: 2 · Check it against the photo
scenes.text: Everything matches the photo this time, and Show me opens the whole letter with those words highlighted, so checking takes a second. AppealPath never trusts the AI's own confidence: in testing, it said it was one hundred percent sure of a sentence it had copied wrong.

scenes.label: 3 · Appeal
scenes.text: The cardiology visit was denied as out of network, so the next step is an appeal. The deadline is quoted from the letter, never calculated, and there's an appeal letter filled in from the letter's own words.

scenes.label: Sample letters
scenes.text: The built-in sample letters, read ahead of time, show the other next steps. This MRI was denied because the office never sent the prior authorization. That's paperwork, so the next step is fix and resubmit, with a script for the call.

scenes.label: Care still ahead
scenes.text: This rehab stay was denied as not medically necessary, a reason that usually leads to an appeal. But the care is still ahead and the doctor says waiting could cause harm, so the rules move it to an urgent review today.

scenes.label: No guessing
scenes.text: Medicare and Medicaid have their own appeal rules, so AppealPath says so the moment you pick one, and doesn't read the letter. A letter with no clear reason gets: call and ask, instead of a guess.

scenes.label: How it decides
scenes.text: Fixed rules pick the next step, each with a source. On twelve clean and fourteen simulated phone photos of the test letters, it chose the right step every time, and the second reader caught every wrong phone number. They're fictional letters, so that's a best case.

scenes.label: En español
scenes.text: It also works in Spanish, and the letter's own words aren't translated, so you can check them against the paper.

scenes.label: AppealPath
scenes.text: AppealPath is a prototype, not medical or legal advice, and it doesn't save your photo or answers. It gets people from a confusing letter to the right phone call.
